name: Cache Top Tube Bag (Velcro)
dims_raw: Small 2.75" wide at stem, 4" tall at stem, 7.75" length (ideal for regular sized iPhone)
dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE. Stored dims are Rockgeist's own figures converted exactly (2.75/4/7.75 in). The elongation test wants len/mid >= 2.0 and gets 1.93, but the 4in height is explicitly quoted AT THE STEM and is the bag's tallest point; the on-bike photo (assets/products/rockgeist/cache-cache-top-tube-bag-velcro-small-2.jpg) shows a wedge that is tall at the stem and tapers to almost nothing at the rear, so the mean height is well under 10.2cm and the real slenderness is far above 2:1. Box 1.4L vs 0.8L rated is right for that taper. No change.

name: Cache Top Tube Bag (Velcro)
dims_raw: XL 2.75" wide at stem, 4.75" tall at stem, 9.25" length (ideal for plus-sized iPhone)
dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE, same reasoning as the Small. Maker's exact figures (2.75/4.75/9.25 in); ratio 1.94 vs a 2.0 threshold. Height is quoted at the stem and the photo shows the bag tapering rearwards. Box 2.0L vs 1.4L rated. No change.

name: Cache Top Tube Bag (Bolt On)
dims_raw: Small 2.75" wide at stem, 4" tall at stem, 7.75" length
dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE. Identical shell to the Velcro version (Rockgeist publishes one size table for both mounts); maker's exact figures, height quoted at the stem, bag tapers rearwards. Photo assets/products/rockgeist/cache-cache-top-tube-bag-bolt-on-small-2.jpg. No change.

name: Cache Top Tube Bag (Bolt On)
dims_raw: XL 2.75" wide at stem, 4.75" tall at stem, 9.25" length
dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE, same as the Velcro XL. Maker's exact figures, ratio 1.94 against a 2.0 threshold, height quoted at the stem on a rearward-tapering wedge. No change.

name: Horton Front Pouch
dims_raw: 11.5" in width, 5.5" in height, and about 3" thick (with roll top all the way rolled); Volume 5.5 L max
dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE on the dimensions - the LITRES are the odd number, not the box. Rockgeist quotes the dimensions explicitly 'with roll top all the way rolled', i.e. the fully compressed, as-ridden state, and separately quotes '5.5 L max' for the roll fully extended. The bar-mounted photo (horton-horton-front-pouch-one-size-2.png) shows the pouch ridden rolled down, matching 29.2 x 14 x 7.6 (3.1L). To reach 5.5L the roll must be let out to roughly 25cm of height. Dims left at the packed figure, which is what the catalogue wants; the rated 5.5L is a max-roll number and is retained as the maker's rating.

name: Dr. Jones Bag
dims_raw: 6" tall, bottom is 10.5" x 3" oval; Volume 9-10L; inner sleeve with drawstring (vertical expansion); bikepacking.com launch spec: 'Capacity 8 liters max, 282 grams'
dims_note: CORRECTED, low confidence. Rockgeist's own two numbers cannot both be true: a 26.7 x 7.6cm oval base 15.2cm tall is 3.1L against a rated 9-10L, and no drawstring sleeve closes a 3x gap. The studio photo on a Jones Loop bar (dr-jones-dr-jones-bag-one-size-1.webp) settles the shape - it is a deep, near-cubic box roughly 30cm across the front face and about 19-20cm tall, with a narrow structured base that flares outward, not a slim 3in-deep pouch; bikepacking.com's launch piece calls it 'a deep bag'. Kept the maker's 10.5in (26.7cm) bar-width; reconstructed height 20cm and depth 15cm so the box lands on the 8L that bikepacking.com's launch spec states (its 282g weight matches Rockgeist's 283g, so it is the same product data). Rockgeist's '6" tall / 3" oval' describes the collapsed structured shell only. Capacity moved 10 -> 8 to the launch figure.

name: Microwave Panniers (Pair)
dims_raw: Holsters are 12" tall, 10" wide, 4" depth. Drybag is 22" x 13.5" when laid flat. 13L per pannier, 26L per set
dims_note: CORRECTED. The stored box was the HOLSTER only (30.5 x 25.4 x 10.2 = 7.9L), which is the rigid carrier, not the loaded pannier. Both mounted photos (microwave-...-3.jpg rear view, -4.jpg on trail) show the grey dry bag sitting well proud of the black holster and bulging past its 4in depth once loaded. Checking the dry bag: a 22 x 13.5in flat panel is a 21.8cm-diameter tube about 16L unrolled, so 13L is reached at roughly 35cm of packed height - consistent with a 30.5cm holster plus around 10cm of bag standing above it. Set the as-mounted box to 25.4 fore/aft (holster width, unchanged) x 40 tall x 14 across, 14.2L, a 1.09 fill on 13L. Height and width are reconstructed from the dry bag geometry plus the photos, not published.

name: Bolt-on Stake Bag
dims_raw: Dimensions: 2" wide, 9" tall. Weight 1.2oz (34g). No volume is published anywhere on the product page.
dims_note: CORRECTED - the LITRES were wrong, not the dims. Re-read the Rockgeist page in full: it publishes no capacity at all for the Stake Bag. The stored 0.8L is identical to the Cache Top Tube Bag Small's 0.8L and is the copy-paste this brand was flagged for. The fork-mounted photo (stake-bolt-on-stake-bag-one-size-1.jpg) shows a slim flat sleeve roughly 2in wide and perhaps 1.5in thick, so real capacity is about 0.4L; a 34g bag cannot hold 0.8L in a 2 x 9in envelope. Dims kept (5.1 mirrors the published 2in width and is an upper bound on thickness); capacity set to 0.4L, derived from the photo and the published 2 x 9in outline.

name: Lezyne Caddy Sack M
dims_raw: Lezyne: Weight 50g, Dimensions 120mm x 147.5mm x 16mm, volume not stated. Retailers: 0.7L capacity, 50g.
dims_note: CORRECTED (axes and depth). The stored record had 1.6cm sitting on the HEIGHT axis and 12cm on the width axis; Lezyne's 16mm is the flat empty thickness of a welded roll-top pouch, a folded measurement rather than a packed one, and it belongs on the across-axis. Remapped to 14.8 long x 12 tall, and filled to the retailer-quoted 0.7L the pouch is about 4cm thick (14.8 x 12 x 4 = 0.71L), so the thickness goes 1.6 -> 4.0. The residual 'too-cubic for downtube' flag is not a dimension error: this is a loose accessory pouch (Lezyne's own page describes no mounting system at all), so the elongated-downtube-bag rule does not apply to it. Left the slot alone because the catalogue vocabulary has no unmounted-accessory slot, but it is worth noting.

name: Lezyne XL-Caddy
dims_raw: Lezyne launch spec (bikepacking.com): 'XL Caddy - Size 420 x 170 x 140 mm, Capacity 7.5 Liters'. Lezyne product page currently lists 330mm x 220mm x 88mm, 424g. Retailers (BIKE24, Modern Bike): 'XL-Caddy Saddle Bag - 7.5L'.
dims_note: CORRECTED - both flags resolved, and this one also proves how to read Lezyne's spec fields. Lezyne's site figure 330 x 220 x 88 is the FLAT-FOLDED bag; its own launch spec, reproduced by bikepacking.com, gives the packed size 420 x 170 x 140 with 7.5L, and two retailers independently list 7.5L. Mapped as a seat pack: len 42 fore/aft, wid 17 across, hgt 14. Box 10.0L on 7.5L rated = 1.33 fill, elongation 2.47. The stored 1.3L is not this bag's volume - it is the Lezyne Stuff Caddy's rating (80 x 60 x 115mm, 1.3L) in the same launch table, another copied attribute.

name: Lezyne Bar Caddy
dims_raw: Lezyne product page: 247g, Dimensions 160.5mm x 250mm x 56.4mm, capacity not stated. Lezyne launch spec via bikepacking.com: 'Bar Caddy - Capacity 7 Liters'. Retailers (Walmart, Boulder Nordic, Stash Cycles) list '7L'.
dims_note: CORRECTED. Lezyne's 160.5 x 250 x 56.4 is the flat-folded panel, established by the XL-Caddy above where the same site field gives a flat figure and Lezyne's launch sheet gives a different packed one. Rated capacity is 7L, not the stored 4L. Lezyne's own on-bike photo (ride.lezyne.com .../Bar_caddy_BigBags-3034...jpg) shows a fat double-ended roll barrel spanning roughly the gap between the brake hoods on a drop bar, about 34cm across with a diameter close to its 16cm flat height. Set 34 x 16.1 x 16.1 = 8.8L box on 7L = 1.26 fill, elongation 2.11. Length and depth are read off that photo, so medium confidence.

name: Lezyne Energy Caddy XL
dims_raw: Lezyne: Capacity 0.8L, Weight 92g, Dimensions 220mm x 65.6mm x 120.3mm
dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE. These are Lezyne's published figures to the millimetre, and unlike the soft roll-top Caddies this is a structured zippered top-tube organiser, so the site's figures are the real packed shape. Ratio 1.83 against a 2.0 threshold; box 1.74L against 0.8L rated, which is the usual margin for a stem-tall bag that tapers rearwards. No change.

name: Drawcord Handlebar Bag
dims_raw: SPECS drawing: 8" (width across bars) x 5" (height) x 4" (depth), plus a 3.5" drawcord extension. VOLUME: 2.6L - 4.9L. WEIGHT: 9.5 oz.
dims_note: CORRECTED capacity only; dims confirmed. Outer Shell keeps its specs in an image, so I pulled the SPECS graphic off their CDN and read it: 8 x 5 x 4in with a 3.5in drawcord collar above. The stored dims are exactly that (20.3 x 12.7 x 10.2 = 2.63L), i.e. the closed bag, and Outer Shell's own 2.6L end of the range matches to two significant figures. The 4.9L is the same bag with the 3.5in collar drawn up (height 8.5in). Set capacity_l to the stated 2.6L so the record is self-consistent with the packed dims; the range stays in the size string.

name: Mega Bar Bag
dims_raw: 8" long, 10" wide, 8.5" tall, with a 6" expandable drawcord section; 10.6L to 18.5L depending on the position of the top flap; 1 lb 15 oz
dims_note: CORRECTED (depth). The stored wid of 14cm had no source. Outer Shell's published figures are 10in wide across the bars, 8.5in tall and 8in long front-to-back, so the fore/aft depth is 20.3cm, not 14. With that fix the box is 25.4 x 21.6 x 20.3 = 11.1L against the rated 10.6L base volume - a 1.05 fill, which is exactly right for an internally-framed bag with a 3D aluminium structure sewn into the panels. The 18.5L is the same bag with the 6in drawcord section let out.

name: Handlebar Harness
dims_raw: Works with bags 4" to 9" in diameter (the only dimensional statement Outer Shell publishes for this product)
dims_note: UNRESOLVED. Outer Shell publishes no dimensions for the harness itself - only the range of dry bag it accepts. The stored 24.1 x 10.2 x 21.6 has no traceable source and I could not corroborate it from the product page, the SPECS graphic (this product's is a photo, not a drawing) or any retailer. Note also that the elongation rule the flag applied is not really meaningful here: this is a mount with liters 0, and its as-mounted envelope is whatever 4-9in dry bag is strapped into it, not a shape of its own. Dims left untouched rather than invented.

name: Oval Dry Bag
dims_raw: 5L: 4" x 7" base, 10" height. Requires 5" from center of handlebars to top of tire.
dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE. Maker's figures map exactly: mounted horizontally in the harness the 10in height becomes the 25.4cm span across the bars and the 4 x 7in base becomes the cross-section, 10.2 tall by 17.8 fore/aft. Ratio 1.43 fails a 1.8 barroll threshold, but that threshold assumes a long thin bar roll; this bag is deliberately short and oval so it clears drop bars and the front tyre (hence the 5in clearance note). Box 4.6L on 5L rated. No change.

name: Oval Dry Bag
dims_raw: 10L: 5" x 8.5" base, 14.5" height. Requires 6" from center of handlebars to top of tire.
dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE. Same mapping as the 5L and the arithmetic closes perfectly: 36.8 x 21.6 x 12.7 = 10.1L against a rated 10L. Ratio 1.70 against a 1.8 threshold is a squat oval by design, not an error. No change.

name: Stem Caddy
dims_raw: 3.5" x 3.5" x 6" with a 2.5" expandable drawcord section; 1.2L to 1.7L capacity; fits a 1L bottle
dims_note: CORRECTED capacity only; dims confirmed. 8.9 x 8.9 x 15.2 = 1.20L, which is Outer Shell's stated 1.2L to the decimal, and letting the 2.5in drawcord collar out takes the height to 8.5in = 1.71L, which is their stated 1.7L to the decimal. So the stored dims are the closed bag and the stored 1.7L was the extended figure. Set capacity_l to the stated 1.2L to match the packed dims; the range stays in the size string.

name: Internode 2 Waterproof
dims_raw: Length 31cm / Height 15cm / MIN. width 5cm / MAX. width 7cm / VOLUME 2 litres / WEIGHT 139 g
dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE. This is the one Internode for which Miss Grape publishes a width, and every number checks out. The studio photo (internode-internode-2-waterproof-2l-1.jpg) measures 1.98:1 length to height, against the published 2.07:1 - the dims are right, the framebag_half threshold of 2.2 is simply too strict for a small triangular road frame bag. Volume also closes: 31 x 15 x 7 = 3.26L box, and the bag is a triangle, so about 0.6 of that is 2.0L, exactly the rating. No change.

name: Internode 4 Waterproof
dims_raw: Length A 42cm / LENGTH C 30cm / HEIGHT B 10cm / HEIGHT D 3cm / VOLUME 4 litres / WEIGHT 198 g
dims_note: CORRECTED width, but flag NOT fully resolved and the reason is Miss Grape's litres. They publish no width for the Adventures Internodes, so the stored 6cm was a placeholder; I set it to 7cm, the published MAX width of the Internode 2 from the same family. The volume still will not close and cannot: the published outline is a wedge with a 42cm top, a 30cm bottom, 10cm at the front and 3cm at the rear, an area of about 234 sq cm, so 4 litres would require roughly 17cm of width - impossible in a front triangle. Cross-checked against the Internode 2, where the same calculation lands within 3% of the rating, so the method is sound and the 4/5/6 ratings are the outliers. Treat Miss Grape's Adventures litres as marketing figures; the real packed volume at 42 x 10 x 7 is nearer 1.8-2.9L. Dry-bag photos (internode-4 studio and on-bike) confirm the long shallow outline.

name: Internode 5 Waterproof
dims_raw: Length A 49cm / LENGTH C 35cm / HEIGHT B 12cm / HEIGHT D 3cm / VOLUME 5 litres / WEIGHT 227 g
dims_note: CORRECTED width 6 -> 7cm, same reasoning as the Internode 4: Miss Grape publishes no width for this bag, 7cm is the published MAX width of the Internode 2 in the same range, and no retailer (bike-packing.de, BIKE24, santafixie) lists a width either - they all repeat only 49 x 12cm. The residual volume shortfall is Miss Grape's optimistic litre rating, not a missing dimension; their published wedge outline holds roughly 3-4L, not 5.

name: Internode 6 Waterproof
dims_raw: Length A 52cm / LENGTH C 37cm / HEIGHT B 14cm / HEIGHT D 4 cm / VOLUME 6 litres / WEIGHT 249 g
dims_note: CORRECTED width 6 -> 7cm, same reasoning as the Internode 4 and 5. The studio photo (internode-internode-6-waterproof-6l-1.jpg) measures about 3.2:1 length to height against the published 3.7:1 and clearly shows the tapered tail, so the published outline is right; only the width was a placeholder and only the litre rating is unreconcilable.

name: MidLoader
dims_raw: SIZE 46 x 12 x 6 cm (4.5 L). Capacity 4.5 L / 275 ci. Tapered outline L1 (top) 46 cm, L2 (bottom) 36 cm, H 12 cm. ART NO TBP-ML6B
dims_note: CORRECTED (width). Topeak's 6cm is the nominal flat width of the empty bag; the product photo (loader-midloader-4-5l-2.png) shows a strongly rounded sausage whose cross-section is nearly circular when packed, not a 6cm slab. The reconciliation is unusually clean: to reach the rated capacity the 4.5L needs 4500/(46x12) = 8.2cm and the 6L needs 6000/(54.5x13.5) = 8.2cm - the same number from two independent sizes, which is what you expect if one shared figure (the flat width) is the thing that is understated. Set wid to 8cm; box 4.4L on 4.5L rated.

name: MidLoader
dims_raw: SIZE 54.5 x 13.5 x 6 cm (6 L). Capacity 6 L / 366 ci. Tapered outline L1 (top) 54.5 cm, L2 (bottom) 44 cm, H 13.5 cm. ART NO TBP-ML6B
dims_note: CORRECTED (width), identical reasoning to the 4.5L: Topeak's 6cm is the flat width and both sizes independently require 8.2cm of packed width to hold their rated capacity. Set wid to 8cm; box 5.9L on 6L rated. The bulging round cross-section is visible in the product photography for both sizes.

name: TopLoader
dims_raw: SIZE 23.5 x 12 x 7 cm / 9.3" x 4.7" x 2.8". Capacity 1 L. ART NO TBP-TL1B
dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE. Topeak's single published size, unmodified. Ratio 1.96 against a 2.0 threshold - a rounding-error miss. The mounted photo (loader-toploader-1l-2.jpg) shows the classic tall-at-the-stem, tapering-to-the-rear wedge, so the 12cm is a maximum height and the mean is much lower; box 1.97L against 1L rated is the normal margin for that taper. No change.

name: Strada Bikepacking Saddle Bag
dims_raw: Width: 24 cm, Depth: 35 cm, Height: 12.5 cm; 9 l.; 400 g
dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE. Refetched the Vincita page and the three figures are confirmed verbatim. The mounted photo (strada-strada-bikepacking-saddle-bag-9l-1.jpg) settles the axis mapping: the side profile of the bag reads about 2.9:1, matching 35 x 12.5, so the 24cm is the across-the-bike width and it is genuinely a wide, shallow mini-duffel strapped under the saddle rather than a tapered bikepacking seat pack. That is why it misses a 1.6 seatpack elongation rule at 1.46 - the rule assumes a tapered tail this bag does not have. Volume closes at 10.5L box on 9L rated. No change.

name: Strada Bikepacking Frame Bag
dims_raw: Width: 35 cm, Depth: 6 cm, Height: 25 cm; 2.6 liters; 0.3 kg
dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE, and the photo is conclusive. The studio shot (strada-strada-bikepacking-frame-bag-2-6l-1.jpg) measures 1.41:1 length to height against the stored 1.40:1 - the numbers describe the bag exactly. It is a true right-triangle half-frame bag that is tall for its length, which is why it misses a 2.2 elongation rule meant for long slim top-tube-hugging bags. Volume also closes on the triangle: half of the 5.25L box is 2.6L, the rating to the decimal. No change.

name: Strada Bikepacking Top Tube Bag
dims_raw: Width: 16 cm, Depth: 6 cm, Height: 9 cm; 0.8 liters; 0.2 kg
dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE. Maker's figures, and the box (0.86L) matches the 0.8L rating almost exactly, which is only possible if all three axes are right. The mounted photo (strada-strada-bikepacking-top-tube-bag-0-8l-1.jpg) shows a small squat flap-top pouch immediately behind the stem, not a long slim gas tank - at 16cm it is simply too short a bag to reach 2:1 over a 9cm height. Threshold too strict. No change.

name: VAUDE Aqua Back Plus
dims_raw: vaude.com: 37 cm (H) x 33 cm (W) x 31 cm (D), volume 51 litres total; 'Delivery includes two panniers for the rear wheel (1 pair), each with a volume of 25.5 liters.' bike-components lists the single pannier as 44 x 33 x 31 cm, 25.5 litres, 1060 g.
dims_note: CORRECTED - the LITRES were the error. The stored 51L is VAUDE's PAIR total; the dimensions are for one bag, so the check was comparing a single bag's box against two bags' capacity. Set capacity_l to VAUDE's own stated 25.5L per bag; box 37.9L on 25.5L = 1.49, normal for a roll-top pannier. Dims left at VAUDE's published H/W/D. One caveat I could not resolve: a 31cm 'depth' is very deep for a rear pannier (17-20cm is typical) and looks like a flat or carton measurement - bike-components repeats VAUDE's own data feed so it is not independent corroboration. Their alternative 44cm height is the roll fully extended; 37cm is the rolled-down figure and is the right one for a packed record.

name: VAUDE Trailfront Cage
dims_raw: Height in cm: 20, Width in cm: 54, Depth in cm: 20; volume 10 liters
dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE on the dims; the SLOT was wrong. The dimensions are VAUDE's own and they are internally consistent: a 10L dry bag 54cm long works out at about 15cm diameter, which sits inside a 20 x 20cm cage envelope. The 54cm only trips a 48cm limit because the product was filed as 'barbag'. VAUDE describe it as a two-part system - a cage that stays clamped to the handlebar plus a removable waterproof dry bag - which is the barroll archetype, and at 54cm it sits directly alongside catalogue peers in that slot (Restrap Holster Bar Bag 54cm, Ortlieb Handlebar-Pack 57.9cm). Reslotted to barroll; dims unchanged.

name: Salsa Cutthroat Stock Frame Bag (58cm)
dims_raw: Rogue Panda product page: 58cm size = 12 liters, 13.4 oz / 380 g (no linear dimensions published). Rogue Panda knowledge base: bags are 'about 2.75 inches wide at the edges, but will expand to 4-5 inches wide in the middle'. Their Cutthroat frame bag guide separately lists 58cm = 14 litres for the full frame bag.
dims_note: CORRECTED, low confidence - reconstructed, not published. Rogue Panda publish no linear dimensions for any stock frame bag. The stored height of 18cm is certainly wrong: this is a FULL frame bag filling the whole main triangle of a 58cm Salsa Cutthroat, and 50 x 18cm is a half-frame outline. Calibrated against the catalogue's own 12L full frame bags - Rockgeist Gravel 52Hz Large at 56 x 36 x 6.5 and WOHO XTouring Full Frame Dry L at 50 x 36 x 8 - and against Rogue Panda's published 2.75in (7cm) edge width, giving 55 x 36 x 7 = 13.9L, a 1.16 fill on 12L that sits in the same band as those peers. Length and height are inferred from that peer set plus the Cutthroat's large front triangle, so treat them as approximate. Note also that Rogue Panda's own Cutthroat guide says 14L for the 58cm while the product page says 12L; kept the product page figure that the catalogue already uses.

name: Zefal Z Traveler 60
dims_raw: Zefal: 320 mm x 180 mm x 220 mm, capacity 20 L / 1220 c.i., 710 g, polyester 840D, universal Velcro mounting. Product title: 'Z TRAVELER 60 - Bike rear bag with modular volume'.
dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE on the dims - the LITRES describe a different configuration. Zefal's own dimensions are 32 x 18 x 22cm (12.7L) and their own capacity is 20L, and Zefal themselves title the product 'bike rear bag with MODULAR volume': the 20L is reached with the fold-out side sections deployed, while 32 x 18 x 22 is the trunk-bag shape with everything stowed. That stowed shape is the correct packed, as-mounted figure for a trunk slot, so dims are unchanged. The rated 20L is retained as Zefal's maximum. Zefal's own page 403s to automated fetches; figures come from the Zefal spec reproduced by BIKE24 and Modern Bike and match the manufacturer listing.

name: Top Tube Bag, Large
dims_raw: 65 cubic inches / 1.1 liters; 7" L x 4" H x 2.5" W
dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE. Banjo Brothers publish both the box and the volume and they agree to 5%: 17.8 x 10.2 x 6.4 = 1.16L against a stated 1.1L / 65 cu in. All three axes cannot be wrong and still produce that agreement. The mounted photo (top-tube-bag-top-tube-bag-large-large-1-1l-1.jpg) shows a short rounded gas-tank pack sitting behind the stem, measuring about 1.6:1 in the image against the published 1.75:1 - it is genuinely a stubby bag, and the 2.0 elongation rule is too strict for a 7in top tube bag. No change.

name: EDC Mini Frame Bag (Large)
dims_raw: VOLUME: Large, 1.4L, true measured. DIMENSIONS: Large, 2.5"W, 10" top, 9.5" bottom, 2" front, 7.5" back
dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE. Venture quote the bag as four edge lengths rather than a box, and read as a wedge the numbers are coherent: a 10in top, 9.5in bottom, 2in front edge and 7.5in rear edge at 2.5in wide is about 1.9L of envelope against a '1.4L true measured' rating, the right margin for a wedge. The bounding box 25.4 x 19.1 x 6.4 is therefore correct. It misses a 2.2 elongation rule at 1.33 because this is a steeply raked wedge that fills the rear corner of the front triangle - it is tall at the seat tube and tapers to nothing forward - not a long slim bag. The only local image for this product is a fabric colour swatch card, so the judgement rests on the maker's four edge lengths. No change.
